title: Longest Substring with K Normal Characters
statement:
Each of the 26 lowercase letters is either **normal** or **special**. This is described by a binary string `status` of length 26: `status[j]` is `'0'` if the letter with index `j` (`'a'` is 0, `'b'` is 1, ..., `'z'` is 25) is normal, and `'1'` if it is special.

You are given a string `S` of lowercase letters and an integer `k`. Find the length of the longest **contiguous substring** of `S` that contains **at most `k` normal characters**. Occurrences count individually: a substring such as `"ff"` with normal letter `f` contains 2 normal characters. There is no limit on the number of special characters.

If no non-empty substring qualifies (for example `k = 0` and every letter of `S` is normal), the answer is `0`.
input_format:
The first line contains the 26-character string `status`.
The second line contains the string `S`.
The third line contains the integer `k`.
output_format: Print the length of the longest valid substring.
constraints: status has length 26 and contains only 0 and 1

examples.explanation: The normal letters are a, f and g. The substring "gir" has only one normal character (the g). No window of length 4 has at most one normal character, so the answer is 3.
All letters are special, so the whole string is valid.
Every letter is normal, so a substring can have at most 2 characters.

hints: Checking every substring costs O(|S|^2) or worse. Notice that if a substring is valid, any substring inside it is valid too.
Use two pointers. Extend the right end one character at a time and keep a count of normal characters inside the window.
When the count exceeds k, move the left end forward until it is at most k again. Track the largest window seen.
brute:
import sys

data = sys.stdin.read().split()
status, s, k = data[0], data[1], int(data[2])
best = 0
n = len(s)
for i in range(n):
    for j in range(i, n):
        sub = s[i:j + 1]
        if sum(1 for ch in sub if status[ord(ch) - 97] == '0') <= k:
            best = max(best, j - i + 1)
print(best)
